drills.q: Your Jace token has 3 loyalty and you are stable on board with a full grip. What is the efficient way to spend it?
a: Three separate -1 surveils
One -3 to draw a card
Hold it as a blocker for their attackers
Nothing - save it for the late game
drills.why: Three surveils cost the same three loyalty as one card. Surveil is the efficient rate and drawing is the luxury rate. Spend -1 three times unless you are flooding out and genuinely need a new card.

drills.q: An opponent has a prepared creature that re-prepares at their upkeep. You hold a 2-mana instant kill spell. When do you cast it?
a: On their upkeep, after the re-prepare trigger
Immediately on your own turn
After they cast the prepared spell
Never - save it for a bigger threat
drills.why: The exiled copy vanishes when the creature leaves the battlefield. Killing it before they cast the copy denies the spell entirely - a clean 2-for-1. Their upkeep is the latest safe window.

drills.q: You control an upkeep-repreparing creature and its prepared copy is a merely break-even play this turn. Do you cast it?
a: Yes - an unspent copy is deleted, not saved
No - hold it for a better window
Only if you have spare mana after your main play
Only if the creature is about to die
drills.why: A creature that is already prepared cannot become prepared again. If you do not spend the copy before your next upkeep, the re-prepare does nothing and the copy is simply wasted. Spend it every turn cycle.

drills.q: Pack 1, pick 8. You are solidly U/B Theorix. A common with 'threshold' text is in the pack alongside a mediocre on-colour creature. Take?
a: The threshold card - it is live in your deck and dead in everyone else's
The creature - threshold is unreliable
Neither, take the best off-colour card
Whichever has the higher mana value
drills.why: Theorix reaches seven cards in the graveyard around turn 5-6; every other deck needs turn 9+. Threshold cards are U/B cards. The bonus is that other drafters cut them, so they come around - but if it is in front of you and you are the Theorix deck, it is a real card.

drills.q: How much is 'empower Jace 3' worth on an otherwise ordinary body?
a: Roughly half a card
Roughly a full extra card
Nothing - the Jace token is a trap
Three cards, one per loyalty
drills.why: Three loyalty converts to one card draw, or three surveils. Call it 0.5-0.7 cards. Worth about 1.3x that in U/B and W/U where the surveils also fire payoffs, and about 0.7x in R/W and B/R where deferred value is worse than a body that attacks now.

drills.q: Which archetype has the biggest swing between draft and sealed?
a: R/G Konstrari - worst in draft, top three in sealed
U/B Theorix - best in both
W/U Fatehold - unchanged
B/R Stingerquill - better in sealed
drills.why: Ramp is card disadvantage in draft when the top end went to eight other drafters. In sealed, pools are full of expensive bombs you otherwise cannot cast, and the aggro punish barely exists. Heartwood also fixes a splash for the best card in your pool.

drills.q: You have no read at all after three picks. Which lane is the correct default?
a: B/G Garruk's Bestiary
B/R Stingerquill
R/G Konstrari
G/U Jace's Mastery
drills.why: Garruk's Bestiary needs the least synergy - good creatures are good creatures - so it has the highest floor in the set. Stingerquill is the lane to avoid unless it is screaming at you.

drills.q: Why is red the weakest colour in this format?
a: Its headline plan points damage at faces instead of creatures
It has no removal at all
It appears in fewer archetypes than the others
Its creatures are undersized
drills.why: Every colour appears in exactly four archetypes. Red's problem is the plan: in a midrange format where killing a prepared creature is a 2-for-1, burning face is paying a real cost for your payoffs - and it runs straight into a lifegain archetype. Red's creature removal is fine; its reach gets over-drafted.

drills.q: Your opponent has a Jace token with 4 loyalty and you have lethal-ish pressure on board. Where do you attack?
a: The player - take the life total
The Jace token, to deny the card advantage
Split evenly between both
Hold back and build a bigger board
drills.why: The Jace token only ticks down - it is a battery, not an engine, and it cannot stabilise their board. Damage to the player is progress toward winning; damage to a shrinking planeswalker usually is not.

drills.q: You are at pack 1 pick 6 and have seen two late Fatehold prepared commons. What does that tell you?
a: W/U is open - it is the most reliable signal in the format
Nothing - uncommons are the real signal
W/U is being cut hard upstream
The pack was weak overall
drills.why: The college prepared creatures are the backbone commons of five archetypes, so lateness on them is a clean read. Gold uncommons mean less than usual here because the Echoed Pair slot floods packs with uncommons.

drills.q: Which prepared spell is the strongest, and why?
a: Fatehold's - it makes a 2/2 and surveils, so enablers are also payoffs
Theorix's - self-mill is the fastest enabler
Stingerquill's - reach wins races
Konstrari's - Heartwood ramps and fixes
drills.why: Fatehold's spell adds a body AND fires the archetype's own scry/surveil payoffs. Most synergy decks have blank enablers and needy payoffs; Fatehold's enablers are the payoffs, so the deck has almost no failure draw.

drills.q: How much interaction should a Reality Fracture draft deck run?
a: 4 or more, with instants preferred
2 is plenty in a creature format
As much as you can, 8+
Only as much as your colours give you
drills.why: 4+ is the target. Instants get a half-grade bump over sorceries here specifically because they let you kill a prepared creature before it casts its copy.

drills.q: In sealed you have a pool with two uncastable 7-drop bombs and passable R/G cards. What do you do?
a: Build R/G Konstrari with Heartwood and 18 lands
Ignore the 7-drops and build the cleanest 2-colour aggro deck
Splash both bombs off two basics
Play a 3-colour goodstuff pile
drills.why: This is exactly the pool Konstrari is for. Heartwood turns uncastable top end into win conditions, sealed games go long enough to get there, and 18 lands is correct when you are ramping to a real top end.

drills.q: Why does the high uncommon count (109 vs 71 commons) change how you draft?
a: You cannot fill a deck from the back half of packs - take playables earlier
Rares matter more than usual
Signals are easier to read
Two-colour decks get worse
drills.why: Roughly 14 commons per colour means the back half of packs is thinner than you are used to. Take playables over speculation earlier, and read signals off commons rather than off late gold uncommons.

drills.q: You empower Jace 2 while you already control a Jace token with 1 loyalty. What happens?
a: Your existing token goes to 3 loyalty
You create a second token with 2 loyalty
You choose which to create; the legend rule applies
Nothing - you cannot empower twice
drills.why: Empower cannot create a second token while you control one; the counters stack on the one you have. The tokens are not legendary, so other effects could make more - but empower alone never will. This is why empower cards never anti-synergise with each other.
